factual_and_methodological.summary: Federal Reserve primary sources confirm the September 16, 2026 12-0 FOMC decision raising the target range to 3.75-4.00%, interest on reserve balances at 3.90%, the standing implementation tools and the standing central-bank swap architecture. The dossier treats international effects as market and liquidity transmission rather than direct authority over foreign policy or private credit allocation.

editorial_publication_readiness.opening: Direct mechanism-led opening; no generic sophistication claims or product-process narration.
editorial_publication_readiness.headings: Headings advance the actor-specific mechanism, constraints, contrary evidence and revision conditions.
editorial_publication_readiness.language_localization: EN and PT-BR are semantically aligned; PT-BR technical prose was localized before approval.
editorial_publication_readiness.cohesion: Argument moves from rights/capability through transmission, constraints and evidence that would revise the assessment.
editorial_publication_readiness.template_meta_qa: No prompt, QA-process, schema, renderer or roadmap leakage detected.

contextual_depth.summary: The dossier distinguishes legal rights, operating capability, transmission, substitutability and institutional constraints rather than relying on scale or reputation.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: At least two analytical tables, one quantitative chart, one causal flow and one mind map in both locales.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: Visuals encode sourced quantities or mechanisms defended in prose and are not combined into a synthetic power score.

contrary_evidence: Market expectations can absorb anticipated policy moves, reducing observed price reactions even when the instrument changes.
Foreign central banks retain authority over domestic implementation, and private intermediaries choose lending and portfolio allocations within their own constraints.
limitations: Cross-border transmission strength varies by currency regime, balance sheet and market structure.
Balance-sheet stocks should not be read as a one-dimensional measure of current monetary stimulus.
notes: Dedicated single-actor Strategic Actors dossier. Primary-source factual core, controlled taxonomy, bilingual parity and visual evidence reviewed; no public bundle for this ID at approval time.

en.title: Federal Reserve: monetary authority, dollar liquidity and the transmission of global financing conditions
en.deck: The Federal Reserve's structural role comes from legal monetary authority over the dollar, a multi-trillion-dollar balance sheet and liquidity backstops whose effects transmit through U.S. and cross-border funding markets.
en.regime: Dollar monetary policy operates through an ample-reserves framework, large securities holdings and standing international liquidity backstops.
en.key_risk: Global transmission can be misdescribed as direct control over private credit or foreign monetary policy.

pt-BR.title: Federal Reserve: autoridade monetária, liquidez em dólar e transmissão das condições financeiras globais
pt-BR.deck: O papel estrutural do Federal Reserve vem da autoridade monetária legal sobre o dólar, de um balanço de vários trilhões e de backstops de liquidez cujos efeitos se transmitem pelos mercados americanos e pelo funding transfronteiriço.
pt-BR.regime: A política monetária do dólar opera por regime de reservas amplas, grande carteira de títulos e backstops internacionais permanentes de liquidez.
pt-BR.key_risk: Transmissão global pode ser descrita incorretamente como controle direto sobre crédito privado ou política monetária estrangeira.

publication.selection_rationale: The Federal Reserve is an active Strategic Actors record with a documented global-financing channel but lacked a dedicated single-actor canonical study.
